text:
maria: Heads-up — reproducible packaging oddity when contributors use Poetry editable installs with the Python SDK. Repro: in sampleapp `poetry install` then `python -c \"import redwood_sdk; import redwood_sdk.asyncio\"` -> ModuleNotFoundError: redwood_sdk.asyncio, while CI wheel contains subpackages.
sam: Sounds like PEP 660/editable backend edge-case. Poetry delegates to pip editable wheel builder; if package discovery metadata is underspecified subpackages can be omitted. Paste your pyproject.toml?
maria: Minimal pyproject: ```toml
[tool.poetry]
name = "redwood-sdk"
version = "0.0.0"
packages = [ { include = "redwood_sdk" } ]
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
python = "^3.8"
``` Layout: `redwood_sdk/__init__.py`, `redwood_sdk/asyncio/__init__.py`, etc. `pip wheel .` is fine; `poetry install` editable often only puts root __init__.py in the env.
josh: Quick checks: 1) confirm not using implicit namespace packages (PEP 420) — that confuses some backends; 2) `poetry self show` — older poetry-core had known editable regressions (e.g. poetry-core 1.6.0 had a bug).
maria: Not using namespace pkgs. All subdirs have __init__.py.
sam: In broken env run: `python -c "import redwood_sdk, pkgutil; print(list(pkgutil.walk_packages(redwood_sdk.__path__)))"` and `python -c "import importlib.metadata as md; print(md.distribution('redwood-sdk').files)"` — this shows what actually landed in the site-packages.
maria: Did that — poetry env shows only root package in pkgutil output and importlib.metadata shows only `redwood_sdk/__init__.py`. `pip install -e .` works (setuptools editable) and lists all subpackages.
josh: Concrete fix: make packaging metadata explicit. Use the table form:```toml
[tool.poetry.packages]
include = "redwood_sdk"
```and add explicit include globs so py.typed and non-code files aren't pruned: under `[tool.poetry]` add `include = ["redwood_sdk/**","py.typed"]`. Also recommend `poetry self update`.
katie: Short-term contributor guidance: prefer `pip install -e .` for local editable devs or `poetry build && pip install dist/*.whl` to mimic CI. Long-term: add CI smoke test that does `poetry install` in clean venv + runs `python -c 'import redwood_sdk.asyncio'` to catch regressions. I'll add a note in onboarding docs. :thumbsup:
dev-bot: CI flagged unrelated macOS ARM wheel-tag error in job 8123: "ERROR: Invalid wheel tag for platform" (log: https://ci.example/8123) — tracking separately.
maria: Opening tiny PR to update pyproject to explicit packages + include py.typed and add contributing note. Will link when ready.
sam: Also add the `pkgutil.walk_packages` and `importlib.metadata` checks to our debugging checklist so others can triage quickly.
josh: Agree. If some contributors still see it after the PR merges, collect: OS, poetry version, pip version, and minimal repro repo. We'll make a reproducible sample if needed.
